newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-FOUR SEEDS FALL, HAARHUIS ADVANCES IN PHILADELPHIA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FOUR SEEDS FALL, HAARHUIS ADVANCES IN PHILADELPHIA.

text.p: Four seeded players fell and -- of the five seeds in action -- only third-seeded Paul Haarhuis of the Netherlands survived the first day of the $714,250 Advanta Championships Monday.
Haarhuis, ranked 25th in the world, defeated Jiri Novak of Czech Republic 6-4 1-6 6-3 in their first-round match.

Fifth-seeded Jason Stoltenberg of Australia, playing in only his second tournament since having surgery on his right forearm in early January, suffered a 6-2 6-4 loss to qualifier Sjeng Schalken of the Netherlands.
Thomas Johansson of Sweden, ranked 65th, stopped eighth-seeded Greg Rusedski of Britain 6-4 6-2 in another first round match.

Rusedski, ranked 35th, came into the match against Johansson having reached the finals of the last two tournaments he played, having finished runner-up to Goran Ivanisevic in Zagreb and Pete Sampras in San Jose.
Fourth-seeded Richey Reneberg of the United States withdrew from the tournament before taking the court with a strained left hip flexor he injured last week in Memphis.
Reneberg's replacement, lucky loser Michael Joyce, lost to wildcard recipient and fellow American Justin Gimelstob 6-0 6-3.
Seventh-seeded Alex O'Brien of the United States fell to 80th-ranked Juan Albert Viloca of Spain 6-2 3-6 6-3.

World number one Pete Sampras and 18th-ranked Jim Courier, the top two seeds here, are the only players in the 32-man Philadelphia draw ranked among the top 20 in the world. Sampras and Courier play their first-round matches Wednesday.

The 31st-ranked Stoltenberg, who lost in the first round of last week's tournament in Memphis, started the day badly. He never delivered a good first serve in the six-point opening game against Shalken.
With service breaks in the first and fifth game, Shalken took a commanding 5-1 lead in the first set.
"I was lucky that in the first game he didn't hit one first serve in," said the 88th-ranked Schalken. "I felt during the match he wasn't 100 percent confident."
The left-handed Rusedski, who never took advantage of five service break point opportunities, was unable to keep his normally potent serve a formidable weapon on the slow indoor hardcourt.
Johansson was able to convert on three of 11 service break chances Rusedski offered -- in the ninth game of the first set, and the first and fifth games of the second set.
"This surface is pretty slow which is why I can return his serve here," said Johansson, a baseline specialist. "If Greg is serving well, I'd have no chance to break his serve."
